To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the n-hexan extracts from the roots and the bark of Elaeodendoron schlechterianum showed strong activity against the Gram-positive bacterial species Bacillus cereus.

some plants from the Bunda district of Tanzania showed promising antibacterial and antifungal activities against the Gram-positive bacterial pathogens Bacillus cereus, Staphylococccus aureus, and the fungal pathogen Candida albicans.

the n-hexan extracts from Elaeodendrion schlechteranum and Balanites aeyptiaca root bark showed antibacterial and antifungal activity, respectively, and the n-hexana extracts from Lannea schwenfurthii, Combetum adenogonium and Ficus sycmorus stem bark exhibited strong antiviral properties.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of potential new sources of natural antimicrobials and antivirals.
the screening for antimicrobial and antiviral activity of 50 extracts of 39 plants belonging to 21 families used in the Tanzanian traditional medicine in Bunda district.
the identification, collection, and screening of medicinal plants from Banda district in the Western zone of the United Republic of Tanzania.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
most plants are active in the treatment of infectious diseases.
the majority of the plants used in the traditional medicine of Bunda district have no or only weak antibacterial, antiviral or antifungal activity.
the plants tested in the present study could be a potential source of antibacterial, antiviral and antifungal agents.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
most of the plants used in traditional medicine in Tanzania are active against microorganisms, but that their use as antiviral agents is limited.
most extracts from Bunda district are active against the Gram-positive microorganisms Bacillus cereus or Staphylococus aureus.
most of these plants are active against bacteria, fungi and viruses and could therefore serve as potential sources of new antimicrobial agents.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of plants as remedies for infectious diseases should be further explored and encouraged.
the plants used by the Bunda community for the treatment of various diseases may be a good source of new antibacterial, antiviral and antifungal compounds.
there is still much to learn about the potential of Tanzanian medicinal plants for the treatment of infectious diseases and the need to conduct further studies on these plants.
